assessment.name: Year 8 RE Autumn assessment
assessment.sections: In your RE lesson in the week of 30 November. 22 multiple choice questions on Smartgrade (bring your Chromebook fully charged) and two 4 mark influence questions. 30 marks in total.
assessment.weighting: How do we know which rules to follow? Rules and laws, the Ten Commandments, Jesus' teachings, Mitzvot and Shariah law.

mock.note: 22 multiple choice questions, like the Smartgrade part. Then answer the two 4 mark questions in the Written practice tab.

group_labels.U: How do we know which rules to follow?

leitner_plan.new: Rules, laws and the Ten Commandments (4)

leitner_plan.quiz: RE mock (22), then both 4 mark questions

cards.title: Rules and laws
cards.question: What is the difference between a rule and a law?
points: Rules are standards of behaviour that are not compulsory for everyone. They are made by families, schools and clubs.
Laws are compulsory standards of behaviour that bind all people living in a community. They are made by the government (Parliament) and enforced by the police and courts.
We have laws to keep everyone safe and to make society fair.
Breaking a rule can lead to a detention, losing a privilege or losing a job. Breaking a law can lead to a fine, losing a licence, community service or prison.
cards.watch_out: Do not say rules and laws are the same. Laws apply to everyone in the country and are enforced by the police; rules apply to a group, such as a school.
cards.hook: Rules for a room, laws for a land.
cards.grade9: Explain why people follow rules even when no one is watching: conscience, respect and, for religious people, belief that God sees everything.

cards.title: Religious laws and government laws
cards.question: What should a religious person do if religious laws and government laws are different?
points: Most of the time religious laws and the law of the land agree, for example do not murder and do not steal.
Christians are taught to Submit to the governing authorities (Romans 13), so they should obey the law.
Some religious people say God's law comes first if a government law is clearly wrong.
Example: people who broke unfair laws peacefully, such as Martin Luther King in the American civil rights movement.
cards.watch_out: Romans 13 is from the New Testament (a letter written by St Paul), not from the Ten Commandments.
cards.grade9: Give both sides: obeying the government keeps order, but some believers argue an unjust law should be challenged peacefully.

cards.title: The Ten Commandments
cards.question: What are the Ten Commandments, and who were they given to?
points: God gave the Ten Commandments to Moses on Mount Sinai (Exodus 20). They are important in Judaism and Christianity.
1 Worship only one God. 2 Do not make or worship idols. 3 Do not misuse God's name. 4 Keep the Sabbath day holy.
5 Honour your father and mother. 6 Do not murder. 7 Do not commit adultery.
8 Do not steal. 9 Do not lie about others (bear false witness). 10 Do not covet (be jealous of) what belongs to others.
cards.watch_out: The first four are about how to treat God (worship). The last six are about how to treat other people.
cards.grade9: Say which commandments are also in UK law (murder, stealing, lying in court) and which are not (keeping the Sabbath).

cards.title: How the Ten Commandments influence Christians
cards.question: How do the Ten Commandments influence Christians today?
points: Keep the Sabbath holy: many Christians go to church on Sunday and rest from work.
Honour your father and mother: Christians respect and care for their parents, for example in old age.
Do not steal and do not lie: Christians try to be honest at school, work and home.
Worship only one God: Christians pray and put God first in their lives.
cards.watch_out: Influence means action. Say what a Christian actually does because of the belief, not just what the commandment says.
cards.grade9: Show that Christians apply the commandments differently: some avoid all work on Sunday, others just go to church.

cards.title: Jesus' Greatest Commandments
cards.question: What did Jesus say were the two greatest commandments?
points: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul and mind.
Love your neighbour as yourself.
Jesus said all the other laws depend on these two (Matthew 22).
Influence: Christians pray and worship (love God) and help others, for example volunteering at a food bank (love neighbour).
cards.watch_out: In the parable of the Good Samaritan Jesus showed that your neighbour is anyone in need, not just the person next door.
cards.hook: Love up (to God), love out (to people).
cards.grade9: Explain why Jesus summed up the law this way: if you truly love God and people, you will keep the other commandments too.

cards.title: How Jesus reinterpreted the old laws
cards.question: How did Jesus reinterpret the old Jewish laws?
points: Old law: Do not do any work on the Sabbath. Jesus: it is right to do good on the Sabbath. He healed people on the Sabbath.
Old law: An eye for an eye. Jesus: Turn the other cheek. Do not take revenge.
Old law: Love your neighbour and hate your enemy. Jesus: Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.
These teachings are in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5).
cards.watch_out: Jesus did not say the old laws were wrong. He said he came to fulfil them, showing their true meaning was about love.
cards.grade9: Explain the influence: Christians may forgive people who hurt them instead of taking revenge, as many victims' families have done.

cards.title: Influence of Jesus' teachings
cards.question: How do Jesus' teachings influence Christians today?
points: Turn the other cheek: Christians try not to take revenge and to forgive.
Love your enemies: Christians may pray for people they disagree with and work for peace.
Doing good on the Sabbath: Christians may help others on Sundays, for example visiting the sick.
Love your neighbour: Christians give to charity, such as Christian Aid, and help people in need.
cards.watch_out: Name the teaching and then the action. A sentence with no action does not show influence.
cards.grade9: Use because to explain why: they do this because Jesus taught that love matters more than following rules strictly.

cards.title: What are the Mitzvot?
cards.question: What are the Mitzvot and what are the two types?
points: Mitzvot (singular: mitzvah) are the commandments or laws in the Torah. There are 613.
Ritual mitzvot are about worshipping God, such as Observe the Sabbath day to keep it holy (Deuteronomy 5:12).
Ethical mitzvot are about how to treat other people, such as To give charity (Deuteronomy 15:11).
The Torah is the first five books of the Jewish scriptures.
cards.watch_out: Ritual means worship of God; ethical means treating people well. Charity is ethical, not ritual.
cards.hook: 613: six, one, three. Ritual is Reverence; Ethical is Everyone else.
cards.grade9: Link the Ten Commandments to the Mitzvot: they are part of the 613.

cards.title: Examples of Mitzvot
cards.question: Which Mitzvot should you know?
points: Observe the Sabbath day to keep it holy (Deuteronomy 5:12): ritual.
To learn Torah and teach it (Deuteronomy 6:7): ritual.
Women should not wear men's clothes (Deuteronomy 22:5): ritual.
To give charity (Deuteronomy 15:11): ethical.
Do not gossip about others (Leviticus 19:16): ethical.
cards.watch_out: Learn one ritual and one ethical example with its reference. Questions often ask for one of each.
cards.grade9: Explain why gossip is treated so seriously: it harms a person's reputation, which cannot easily be repaired.

cards.title: Influence and importance of the Mitzvot
cards.question: How do the Mitzvot influence Jews, and why are they important?
points: Orthodox Jews follow all the mitzvot because they believe they were given by God.
Reform Jews do not follow all the mitzvot; they choose how to apply them to modern life.
Influence: keeping Shabbat, reading the Torah, sending children to religious schools, giving to charity, some women wearing long skirts and dresses.
Importance: they guide Jews on how to live a good life and are part of the covenant (promise) between God and the Jewish people. Many Jews believe disobeying them brings punishment.
cards.watch_out: Not all Jews practise in the same way. Say Orthodox or Reform Jews, or some Jews, rather than all Jews.
cards.hook: Orthodox: all of them. Reform: re-form them for today.
cards.grade9: Use the word covenant to explain why the mitzvot matter: keeping them is keeping the promise to God.

cards.title: What is Shariah law?
cards.question: What is Shariah law and where does it come from?
points: Shariah law is Islamic law. It guides how Muslims should live.
Two primary sources: the Qur'an (the word of Allah) and the Hadith (sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad).
Secondary sources: scholars agreeing together (ijma) and reasoning by comparison (qiyas), used when the primary sources do not answer a new question.
Shariah covers worship, food, family life, business and charity.
cards.watch_out: Shariah is not only about punishments. Most of it is about everyday life, such as prayer, food and charity.
cards.hook: Q and H first: Qur'an and Hadith.
cards.grade9: Explain why secondary sources are needed: new issues, such as modern technology, are not mentioned directly in the Qur'an.

cards.title: Shariah law: teachings, influence and importance
cards.question: What do Qur'an teachings in Shariah say, and how do they influence Muslims?
points: The Qur'an calls intoxicants such as alcohol an abomination to avoid. Influence: Muslims do not drink alcohol. Importance: it can cause poor judgement.
Establish prayer and give Zakat. Influence: Muslims start giving Zakat (2.5% of savings) once they earn money. Importance: it helps the needy and poor.
The Qur'an teaches not to approach unlawful sexual relationships. Influence: sex should only happen within marriage. Importance: marriage is encouraged.
Shariah helps Muslims live in a way that pleases Allah.
cards.watch_out: Zakat is a set amount of savings (2.5%), not any donation. Extra voluntary charity is called sadaqah.
cards.grade9: Compare: like the ethical mitzvot and Jesus' teaching to love your neighbour, Zakat puts care for others into action.

cards.title: How to write a 4 mark influence answer
cards.question: How do you answer Explain two ways a belief influences religious people today?
points: The question always wants TWO reasons, and each must be explained (2 marks each).
Reason: Some Christians believe ...
Explain: This influences them to ... because ...
Influence means action: say what they do.

example.heading: Model answer: two ways the Ten Commandments influence Christians
lines: Some Christians believe they should keep the Sabbath day holy. This influences them to go to church on Sunday because they want to spend the day with God.
Some Christians believe they should honour their father and mother. This influences them to care for their parents in old age because God commanded it.

cards.watch_out: Two reasons without explanation only get 2 out of 4. Always add the because.
cards.hook: R E, R E: Reason, Explain, twice.
cards.grade9: For contrasting beliefs questions, give two different views, such as Orthodox and Reform Jews.

cards.title: Key numbers and quotes
cards.question: Can you recall the key facts for the RE assessment?
points: 613 mitzvot. 10 commandments: first 4 about God, last 6 about people. Given to Moses.
Jesus' two Greatest Commandments: love God; love your neighbour as yourself.
Jesus: turn the other cheek; love your enemies; do good on the Sabbath.
Shariah: Qur'an and Hadith. Zakat 2.5%. No alcohol.
Submit to the governing authorities (Romans 13).
cards.watch_out: Learn one quote for each religion and the action it leads to.

written.q: Explain two ways the Ten Commandments influence Christians today.
model: Reason: Christians believe they should keep the Sabbath holy (1)
Explain: so they go to church on Sunday and rest, because they want to spend the day with God (1)
Reason: Christians believe they should not steal or lie (1)
Explain: so they try to be honest at school and work, because God commanded it (1)

written.q: Explain two ways Shariah law influences Muslims today.
model: Reason: Shariah teaches Muslims to give Zakat (1)
Explain: so they give 2.5% of their savings to help the poor and needy (1)
Reason: the Qur'an teaches that intoxicants should be avoided (1)
Explain: so Muslims do not drink alcohol, because it can cause poor judgement (1)

written.q: Explain two contrasting ways Jews follow the Mitzvot.
model: Because they believe the mitzvot were given directly by God, for example strictly keeping Shabbat (1)
Reform Jews do not follow all the mitzvot (1)
Because they believe they can be applied to modern life, so they choose which to follow (1)

written.q: Explain two ways Jesus' teachings influence Christians today.
model: Jesus taught turn the other cheek (1)
So Christians try to forgive and not take revenge (1)
Jesus taught love your neighbour as yourself (1)
So Christians help others, for example volunteering at a food bank (1)

exam_tips.timing: Smartgrade: 22 questions, about 1 minute each. Then spend about 8 minutes on each 4 mark question.
section_a: Read all four options before choosing.
section_b: Two reasons, each explained with an action.
Use the sentence starters Some Christians believe and This influences them to.
Add a quote if you can, such as Love your neighbour as yourself.
grade9: For any rule ask who made it, why, and when it might fail.
Is a rule still right if following it causes harm? Use a question like this to argue both sides, as Jesus did when he healed on the Sabbath.

mcq.q: What is a rule?
mcq.a: A standard of behaviour that is not compulsory for everyone
w: A punishment given by a court
mcq.e: Rules are made by groups such as schools and families.

mcq.q: What is a law?
mcq.a: A compulsory standard of behaviour for everyone in a community
mcq.e: Laws bind all people and are enforced by the police and courts.

mcq.q: Who makes laws in the UK?
mcq.e: Parliament passes laws for the whole country.

mcq.q: Which is a possible consequence of breaking a law?
mcq.e: Laws can lead to fines, community service or prison.

mcq.q: Which is a possible consequence of breaking a school rule?
mcq.e: School rules are enforced by the school.

mcq.q: Why do we have laws?
mcq.a: To keep people safe and society fair
mcq.e: Laws help provide for general safety.

mcq.q: Which teaching tells Christians to follow government laws?
mcq.e: Romans 13 in the New Testament.

mcq.q: Who received the Ten Commandments?
mcq.e: On Mount Sinai.

mcq.q: What do the first four commandments focus on?
mcq.e: The last six are about other people.

mcq.q: Which is one of the Ten Commandments?
mcq.e: Number 8.

mcq.q: What does covet mean?
mcq.a: To be jealous of and want what belongs to someone else
mcq.e: The tenth commandment is do not covet.

mcq.q: Which commandment might lead a Christian to go to church on Sunday?
mcq.e: The Sabbath is a holy day of rest and worship.

mcq.q: Which commandment might lead a Christian to look after their parents in old age?
mcq.e: Honouring parents includes caring for them.

mcq.q: What does influence mean in an RE answer?
mcq.a: The action a person takes because of a belief
w: The date a law was written
mcq.e: Influence = action.

mcq.q: What is one of Jesus' Greatest Commandments?
w: Do not work on the Sabbath
mcq.e: The other is love God with all your heart.

mcq.q: How did Jesus reinterpret An eye for an eye?
mcq.e: Jesus taught not to take revenge.

mcq.q: How did Jesus reinterpret Love your neighbour and hate your enemy?
mcq.a: Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you
mcq.e: From the Sermon on the Mount.

mcq.q: What did Jesus do on the Sabbath that showed it was right to do good?
mcq.e: Doing good is allowed on the Sabbath.

mcq.q: Which parable shows that your neighbour is anyone in need?
mcq.e: A Samaritan helped an injured stranger.

mcq.q: How might Turn the other cheek influence a Christian?
mcq.a: They forgive instead of taking revenge
mcq.e: Influence is an action.

mcq.q: In which part of the Bible is the Sermon on the Mount?
mcq.e: Matthew's Gospel, chapters 5 to 7.

mcq.q: How many mitzvot are there?
mcq.e: They are found in the Torah.

mcq.q: What are ritual mitzvot about?
mcq.e: Keeping the Sabbath is a ritual mitzvah.

mcq.q: What are ethical mitzvot about?
mcq.e: Giving charity is an ethical mitzvah.

mcq.q: Which is an ethical mitzvah?
w: Learn the Torah and teach it
mcq.e: Leviticus 19:16 is about treating others.

mcq.q: Which is a ritual mitzvah?
mcq.a: Observe the Sabbath day to keep it holy
mcq.e: Deuteronomy 5:12 is about worship.

mcq.q: Which Jews follow all of the mitzvot?
mcq.e: Reform Jews choose how to apply them.

mcq.q: What is a covenant?
mcq.a: A promise between God and people
mcq.e: Keeping the mitzvot is part of the covenant.

mcq.q: What are the two primary sources of Shariah law?
w: The Ten Commandments and the Qur'an
mcq.e: The Hadith are sayings and actions of the Prophet.

mcq.q: What is Zakat?
mcq.a: Giving a set part (2.5%) of savings to the poor
mcq.e: It is one of the Five Pillars.

mcq.q: When do Muslims start giving Zakat?
mcq.a: Once they are earning money and have savings
mcq.e: It helps the less fortunate.

mcq.q: Why do Muslims avoid alcohol?
mcq.a: The Qur'an calls intoxicants an abomination
w: It is only banned on Fridays
mcq.e: It can cause poor judgement.

mcq.q: What is ijma?
mcq.a: Scholars agreeing together on a law
mcq.e: It is a secondary source of Shariah.

mcq.q: How many reasons does a 4 mark influence question need?
mcq.e: 2 marks for each explained reason.

mcq.q: Which sentence shows influence?
mcq.a: This influences them to give to charity because Jesus taught love your neighbour.
mcq.e: Influence must be an action with a reason.

vocab.example: The fifth commandment is to honour your father and mother.

vocab.meaning: A Jewish commandment from the Torah (plural: mitzvot)
vocab.example: Giving charity is an ethical mitzvah.

vocab.meaning: A special promise or agreement between God and people
vocab.example: Jews believe the mitzvot are part of the covenant with God.

vocab.meaning: Islamic law, based on the Qur'an and Hadith
vocab.example: Shariah guides Muslims in prayer, food and charity.

vocab.meaning: Giving 2.5% of savings to the poor, one of the Five Pillars of Islam
vocab.example: Muslims pay Zakat once they have enough savings.

vocab.meaning: A holy day of rest and worship
vocab.example: Many Christians go to church on the Sabbath.

vocab.meaning: The effect a belief has on how someone acts
vocab.example: The influence of Jesus' teaching is that Christians forgive others.

vocab.meaning: To want something that belongs to someone else
vocab.example: The tenth commandment says do not covet your neighbour's things.

vocab.meaning: To treat people cruelly because of who they are or what they believe
vocab.example: Jesus taught his followers to pray for those who persecute them.
